transcript_body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll walk through the Redwood Operation Lens today, focusing on tracing and how we do graceful fallbacks. I'm Maya, AE on the account. With me is Luca, our systems SE.
[00:12] Jonah Patel: Thanks, Maya. On our side I'm Jonah. We have Rita from SRE, Samir for security, Priya our PM, and Devon an ML engineer.
[00:22] Maya Chen: Awesome. Quick ask: Rita, when we talk about request playback, are you mostly interested in end-user repros or infra-level traces?
[00:32] Rita Gomez: Both really, we need to be able to take a user ticket and map it back through the token path — like, what model served it, whether there was a fallback to smaller model, and where latency spiked.
[00:44] Luca Moretti: Totally. In the Console we show a request timeline with per-token latency bars, the model variant used per segment, and any cache hits. You can scrub and replay. Bear in mind the transcript generation isn't perfect, sometimes the names get munged in autosub, but the request ids are exact.
[00:58] Priya Menon: Can you show us a full replay? A ticket yesterday had a 2.2s tail latency and the user quote had truncated output.
[01:08] Luca Moretti: Sure — pulling up a sample. Okay this one is synthetic but similar.
[01:17] [01:17] Luca Moretti: (screen share) Here's the request timeline. You can see initial model selection, then a drop to the fallback variant at 0.9s due to a transient OOM on the host. The Console marks that event as 'fallback: capacity' and attaches the logs.
[01:33] Devon Lee: Wait, how do you distinguish between a deliberate routing policy vs an automatic fallback?
[01:39] Maya Chen: Great question. We annotate the timeline: "policy routed" vs "automatic fallback". Policies are user-configured — like prefer low-latency model for premium tier — automatic fallbacks happen when the runtime detects errors or degraded kernels.
[01:52] Samir Khan: On security: does replay expose raw prompt text? We need to ensure PII control and auditability.
[02:00] Anika Rao: By default Console masks PII in transcripts and you can enable strict retention that redacts full prompts from the UI; raw logs remain encrypted and access-controlled with RBAC/KMS.
[02:12] Samir Khan: How does that integrate with our KMS? We're on HashiCorp Vault + Cloud KMS.
[02:18] Maya Chen: We support customer-managed keys via KMS and HSM integrations. The control plane can be configured to encrypt logs and model artifacts with your key; audit logs show key usage events. We'll send the integration notes.
[02:30] [02:30] Jonah Patel: Can the Console show kv cache hits for a given request? We suspect our prefix-hot routes are under-cached.
[02:38] Luca Moretti: Yes — the request detail shows kv cache state: hit/miss percentage, cache lookup latency, and the cached tokens returned. We also show a visualization of prefix cache snapshotted at request start; if there was a miss we show the fallback path.
[02:52] Rita Gomez: And how is cache warming recommended? We're worried about cold starts and spikes.
[02:58] Luca Moretti: We have an Optimize suggestion in the Console — it analyzes workload and recommends batch sizes, pre-warming TTLs, and quantization profile tradeoffs. Note recommendations are based on historical traces, so the more traffic you share the better the suggestions.
[03:14] Priya Menon: You mentioned quantization — is that something that affects tracing fidelity?
[03:19] Luca Moretti: Not directly; quantization affects model performance and occasionally sequence-level latencies. The traces capture timestamped events irrespective of quantization.
[03:27] [03:27] Devon Lee: If there's an OOM and you fall back to smaller model, do you have token continuity? Like KV cache keys mapping across model variants?
[03:37] Luca Moretti: We attempt KV cache migration heuristics when model architectures are compatible. If incompatible, the fallback will regenerate but the Console flags that the output may differ and shows diff highlights.
[03:48] Jonah Patel: That diff view — can we export it? Our compliance team wants diffs for audit trails.
[03:54] Maya Chen: Yes, exportable as JSON + human readable. We keep an immutable audit trail with request ids, delta metrics, and the associated decision points.
[04:04] Samir Khan: Audit trail storage — retention and access controls?
[04:08] Anika Rao: Retention is configurable at the org level; for Private deployments you can choose on-prem retention policies. Access is via SSO + scoped roles; all API calls are logged.
[04:18] Rita Gomez: Can you demo an incident flow? For example, a request that escalated to latency SLAs and how SRE would root cause with the Console.
[04:25] Luca Moretti: Sure. I'll simulate a high-latency event.
[04:30] [04:30] Luca Moretti: (simulating) At T+0 you see request bursts. At T+10s several host kernels log 'cuda mem alloc failed' — the runtime moves some requests to a lighter-weight model and throttles batch size. The Console generates an incident card with recommended remediation: increase burst pool, enable priority lanes for critical customers, or configure automatic fallback thresholds.
[04:50] Rita Gomez: Interesting — who owns those recommendations? Are they auto-executed?
[04:55] Maya Chen: They are suggestions. For Hosted customers you can enable AutoRemediate which will attempt safe config changes; for Dedicated/Private we only surface runbook steps and operators execute them.
[05:06] Priya Menon: On the Hosted vs Dedicated decision — we're balancing cost and compliance. Can you summarize the key differences for observability and SRE workflows?
[05:16] Maya Chen: Hosted gives fastest onboarding and automatic kernel choices, plus managed burst pools. Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and network isolation; Private gives total control of keys and on-prem logs. Observability features are the same but integrations and KMS control differ — Dedicated/Private allow customer KMS and VPC flow logs in your tenancy.
[05:34] Jonah Patel: We run a HIPAA-ish workflow. If we do Dedicated, can we get raw request logs into our S3 behind VPC?
[05:42] Anika Rao: Yes, with Dedicated we can push logs to your S3 endpoint or a SIEM over a private peering. Encryption uses your keys if requested.
[05:50] Samir Khan: Ok. A few nitty details: SAML vs OIDC, session timeouts, and API token rotation — are these configurable?
[05:59] Maya Chen: SSO supports SAML and OIDC; session lifetime and token rotation are configurable via the Admin console. We also log changes to auth config in the audit log.
[06:09] [06:09] Rita Gomez: Back to traces: sometimes we see gaps in the logs — like missing KV reads — could that be sampling?
[06:16] Luca Moretti: Yes, sampling can drop lower-priority traces. We surface sampling rates on the Console and allow you to set full-capture for specific customer IDs or request patterns. For heavy workloads we recommend targeted full-capture.
[06:28] Devon Lee: Does full-capture add much cost?
[06:31] Luca Moretti: It increases storage/ingestion costs proportionally; Optimize can show cost delta.
[06:36] Jonah Patel: Any competitor pitfalls we should be aware of? We looked at vendor X and saw blackbox traces.
[06:42] Maya Chen: Right — some providers only provide aggregated metrics. We aim to provide per-request playback with immutable request IDs so you can trace end-to-end.
[06:53] Priya Menon: Can you walk through an example where the Console helped find a bad prompt causing hallucinations?
[06:59] Luca Moretti: Yeah — we had a case where a prompt truncation combined with KV cache misalignment produced hallucinated completion. The Console timeline showed that the cache returned stale prefix chunk, and the diff view highlighted that the earlier prompt token stream was mismatched. The fix was a cache invalidation policy tied to content-versioning.
[07:23] Samir Khan: Content-versioning — is that something Redwood enforces or we manage?
[07:27] Maya Chen: It's customer-configurable; we provide hooks to include content hashes in cache keys and the Console will surface mismatches.
[07:35] Rita Gomez: For the POC, we want to run a replay test using our anonymized traffic — what is the easiest way to ingest sample request IDs and traffic?
[07:44] Maya Chen: You can either share request IDs with retention on your side and grant Redwood read-only access, or upload a redacted request bundle via the Console upload tool. We'll sign an NDA and follow your data handling rules.
[07:56] Jonah Patel: About the replay, can it be run against a different model variant to test fallback behavior?
[08:02] Luca Moretti: Yes, the replay tool supports variant substitution and will report delta metrics. It simulates the runtime decisions and gives an estimate of latency/cost changes.
[08:12] Devon Lee: Is there an API to kick off replays so we can automate canaries?
[08:16] Maya Chen: There is — the Replayer API can be called with a bundle and a target model variant.
[08:22] [08:22] Priya Menon: Great. A couple security follow-ups: will you send the KMS integration notes and also the SOC2 page?
[08:29] Maya Chen: Yes. I'll follow up after call.
[08:33] Samir Khan: About RBAC — can we restrict Console playback so only SREs see raw prompts while PMs see redacted summaries?
[08:40] Anika Rao: Yes, role-level UI controls let you hide prompt content and only show redacted text or metadata. Audit logs show who accessed raw content.
[08:49] Rita Gomez: A practical question: what diagnostics do you need from us to reproduce the 2.2s tail latency?
[08:56] Lucas? [sic] Devon Lee: We can provide sample request IDs and a short trace window. We'll also share some metric snapshots from our overlaying infra.
[09:04] Maya Chen: Perfect — send over the IDs. Luca will ask for a CSV.
[09:10] [09:10] Luca Moretti: I'll note that down. Also a note on mis-transcriptions: sometimes "KV" gets written as "K V" in auto transcripts, and model names like "redwood-dyno" might show up incorrectly.
[09:21] Jonah Patel: Understood. For the POC scope — we want to validate observability, fallback fidelity, and cost tradeoffs. Can you propose a minimal POC plan?
[09:30] Maya Chen: Proposal: 2-week pilot. Week 1: integrate request forwarding and set retention; run 3k replay tests; run KV cache stress emulation. Week 2: run canary replays against smaller variants to measure delta and generate reports. We'll present a post-mortem and recommendations.
[09:48] Priya Menon: Timeline-wise we want this in February — is that feasible?
[09:53] Maya Chen: Yes, if we kick off the week of Feb 9 we can deliver results by Feb 23.
[09:58] Rita Gomez: Fine. A small ask — can Console show a heatmap of per-route latency percentiles?
[10:05] Luca Moretti: It does — per-route p50/p95/p99 heatmap, and you can filter by model variant and time window.
[10:14] Samir Khan: For compliance, will you provide log-export scripts? We prefer IaC.
[10:18] Anika Rao: We have Terraform modules and Log Export templates for S3/SIEM sinks. We'll share repo links.
[10:25] Devon Lee: One more: can the Console correlate infra events (like host reboots) with request spikes?
[10:30] Luca Moretti: Yes, it ingests host telemetry and correlates events by time-series; you can overlay host logs on the request timeline.
[10:38] [10:38] Jonah Patel: We're worried about the cost of full-capture on production. If we do targeted full-capture for high-value customers only, how granular can we be?
[10:47] Maya Chen: You can set filters by customer id, route, or metadata tags. Granularity is per-request.
[10:52] Priya Menon: Ok that helps. Another smaller question: fallback notifications — can we hook those into PagerDuty?
[10:58] Anika Rao: Yes — alerting supports PagerDuty, Slack, and webhooks.
[11:03] Rita Gomez: Great. I have one more: when a fallback occurs, does the Console automatically surface the confidence delta in the response?
[11:10] Luca Moretti: We compute a quality delta metric where possible (e.g., BLEU-ish or embedding cosine to baseline) and show a confidence band. But for open-ended tasks it's heuristic.
[11:22] Priya Menon: That metric could be useful for our ML team.
[11:25] Devon Lee: Agreed. We'll want the raw outputs to compute our own metrics.
[11:30] Maya Chen: You can export raw outputs subject to your retention settings; for PII you can request de-identification.
[11:36] Jonah Patel: Cool. Any questions from your side, Maya?
[11:40] Maya Chen: Nope, just to confirm action items. We'll follow up SOC2, KMS notes, and Luca will run the KV tests. We'll also draft a POC plan doc and share later today.
[11:51] Priya Menon: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[11:55] Samir Khan: Thanks all.
[11:58] Maya Chen: Thanks, bye!
[12:02] (call ends, recording stopped)

Notes on transcript fidelity: There were a few speaker label swaps in the first 10 minutes and some auto-caption errors for acronyms (KMS, KV). Customer provided some request IDs post-call via email.
